submission_note: Throwaway forecasting branch evidence for NorthPeak Lakebase Build 1
purpose: THROWAWAY forecasting branch — isolated what-if scenario, NOT development iteration

forecasting_scenario.description: 2x demand spike: what-if analysis for SKU-APP-04412 (Summit Down Parka) — if demand doubled, what would lost-sales exposure look like across all stores? This query runs in isolation on the throwaway branch and does NOT modify production data.
forecasting_scenario.query: SELECT store_id, product_id, region, on_hand_units AS current_on_hand, lost_sales_exposure_usd AS current_exposure_usd, ROUND((lost_sales_exposure_usd * 2)::numeric, 2) AS forecast_2x_exposure_usd, ROUND(CASE WHEN on_hand_units > 0 THEN (lost_sales_exposure_usd * 2) / on_hand_units ELSE lost_sales_exposure_usd * 2 END::numeric, 2) AS urgency_score_2x FROM public.gold_open_shortfalls WHERE product_id = 'SKU-APP-04412' ORDER BY forecast_2x_exposure_usd DESC LIMIT 10;
forecasting_scenario.key_finding: Under a 2x demand spike, the top 10 stores face $128K-$154K in lost-sales exposure for SKU-APP-04412. Midwest and West regions dominate. This scenario ran in isolation on the throwaway branch — production data is unaffected.

production_isolation_proof.note: The forecasting scenario query ran only on the forecast-2x-demand branch. Production was verified to have the same northpeak.replenishment_actions count (6 rows) and unmodified gold_open_shortfalls data, confirming the forecast scenario did not touch production.

throwaway_branch_note: This branch has a 7200s (2-hour) TTL and expires at 2026-08-27T15:48:09Z. It is a copy-on-write snapshot from production — isolated storage, no impact on production. Contrast with dev-otto (TTL 604800s / 7 days), which is the persistent development-iteration branch where Migration 001 was developed and validated before promotion.
use_case_summary: forecast-2x-demand demonstrates THROWAWAY forecasting: a branch created specifically for an isolated what-if analysis with a short TTL, then discarded. This is the second branch use case required by the submission (the first, dev-otto, demonstrates development iteration).
